Synthetic calibration set with three human raters

Source: R/data.R
synthetic_gold.Rd

A 200-item synthetic set of support-style question/answer items, each rated Incorrect / Partial / Correct by three simulated human raters. It is sized so that an audit can reach a verdict rather than stop at INDETERMINATE, and it is the input for the README's end-to-end run. Every label is planted: a true label was drawn per item, the answer text written to match it (correct answers name a place and an action, partial answers hedge, incorrect answers deflect), and each rater is the truth with a 6% chance of an adjacent-level slip. The text is templated from 24 questions, so no row is a real ticket; what is independent across rows is the draw of the label and of each rater's error. Inputs are at most 180 characters, so a judge whose behaviour changes above 240 characters is moved by the verbosity probe's filler and not by the shorter framing prefixes of the other probes. Not a benchmark and not a basis for any deployment decision.

Usage

synthetic_gold

Format

A tibble with 200 rows and 6 columns:

id

Character item identifier, "syn-001" to "syn-200".

input

Character. The question and candidate answer presented to the judge, formatted as "Question <n>: ...\nAnswer: ...".

target

Character. The grading criterion; the same sentence for every item.

rater_1, rater_2, rater_3

Simulated human ratings, ordered factors with levels I < P < C.

Source

Generated by data-raw/synthetic_gold.R with a fixed seed.

Examples

synthetic_gold
#> # A tibble: 200 × 6
#>    id      input                                  target rater_1 rater_2 rater_3
#>    <chr>   <chr>                                  <chr>  <ord>   <ord>   <ord>  
#>  1 syn-001 "Question 1: How do I upgrade my plan… Does … C       C       C      
#>  2 syn-002 "Question 2: Is two-factor authentica… Does … I       I       I      
#>  3 syn-003 "Question 3: Can I get a refund for l… Does … P       P       I      
#>  4 syn-004 "Question 4: Why does my import fail?… Does … C       P       C      
#>  5 syn-005 "Question 5: What are your support ho… Does … P       P       P      
#>  6 syn-006 "Question 6: Does the API have rate l… Does … C       C       C      
#>  7 syn-007 "Question 7: Why is my dashboard slow… Does … C       C       C      
#>  8 syn-008 "Question 8: How do I reset my passwo… Does … C       C       C      
#>  9 syn-009 "Question 9: What file types can I up… Does … I       I       I      
#> 10 syn-010 "Question 10: How do I upgrade my pla… Does … P       P       P      
#> # ℹ 190 more rows
calibrate_judge(
  synthetic_gold,
  human_cols = c("rater_1", "rater_2", "rater_3"),
  judge = function(data) {
    tibble::tibble(.item_id = data$.item_id, label = rep("C", nrow(data)))
  },
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  id_col = "id",
  label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
  scale = "ordinal",
  n_boot = 100,
  seed = 1
)
#> 
#> ── yourhonor judge calibration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 200 usable items of 200 - descriptive judge-vs-human agreement:
#> • cohen_kappa: -0.00 [-0.00, -0.00] (slight)
#> • krippendorff_alpha: -0.22 [-0.27, -0.18] (poor)
#> • gwet_ac2: 0.68 [0.61, 0.76] (substantial)
#> 84 disagreements; inspect `confusion_metrics()` before use.
#> Human reliability benchmark (3 raters): gwet_ac2 = 0.92.
#> ℹ No deployment decision is implied; call report() with a policy to assess one.
